column1: # SWB.PRG partitioned into subsystems, for tools/hw_portability.py --subsystems.
# `lo<TAB>hi<TAB>name`, matched against a function's ENTRY address, FIRST MATCH WINS — so the
# specific ranges come first and the catch-all last. Several disjoint ranges may share a name.
# Boundaries follow the region table and the function clusters in ../notes/architecture.md;
# every address is a RUNTIME address (base 0x3f8).
# Each `hi` is the `body_end` `../out/hw_scan.tsv` records for the LAST function in the range, so
# a range ends exactly where the next function begins and no entry address is claimed twice.
# ONE range departs from that rule and says so on the spot: `0x2b5a..0x2bc8`, where Ghidra has no
# function at all and the `hi` is read off the reconstructed bodies instead.
# ONLY CODE BELONGS HERE. A range is matched against a function ENTRY, so a pure data block can
# never be claimed by one: the message-pointer table at `$a09c` that `text_run_message_box` walks
# (batch 9) sits inside ../notes/architecture.md's DATA row `$989c..$a271` and is deliberately
# absent, as are the actor tables at `$996c`/`$9bd0`/`$9e34` and the screen array at `$98ec`.
# The same reasoning keeps three data blocks that sit INSIDE CODE regions out of the ranges below:
# the eight 32-byte palettes at `$fc46..$fd46` that `stage_load_window` indexes, the scratch and
# stage pointers at `$fe0c..$fe1e`, and the three tile-$33 words at `$1514..$151a`.
0x3f8
# The scroll ENGINE's request raiser (batch 5): `$d28` reads the followed object's position and
# raises the queue entries `bg_scroll_run_queue` ($7522) drains. One function, 78 bytes.
0xd28
# The COLLISION MAP (batches 10-11): the two-dimensional tile grid the actors walk on, and every
# routine that reads or writes it. Three disjoint ranges, each tiling its F rows exactly:
#   `$10a2..$1208` — the two horizontal steps, `actor_step_left_against_map` / `_right_`, which
#     refuse to enter a tile-$1 cell and retry a pixel at a time (mirrors, not a parametrisation);
#   `$1334..$1514` — `actor_fall_and_settle` (the tier above the probes), the shared cell lookup
#     `$13be`+`$13c8` (the first FALLS THROUGH into the second, no `rts` of its own), and the two
#     settles `$1400` (tile $23) / `$1492` (tile $1 or $2). It also claims `$14d6`
#     `actor_accelerate_fall`, which is an actor routine by role but is physically ENCLOSED in
#     `$1492`'s body (`blt.w $14d6` at `$14c0` jumps into it, and Ghidra's body_end for `$1492` is
#     `$1514`), so splitting it out would charge one function body to two subsystems;
#   `$1af0..$1b46` — `map_stamp_block`, the only writer, stamping a 2x2 block of tile codes.
# Nine F rows, 924 bytes, all reconstructed and green. `$1ab4` is deliberately outside: nothing
# is established about it. `$1514..$151a` is the three tile-$33 words, i.e. data.
0x1af0
# The actor LIFECYCLE (batches 10 and 13), joining the entry tier and projections below:
#   `$1b68..$1bb4` — the two slot allocators, byte-identical bar two operand words, whose pools
#     (slots 3..11 and 13..18) meet either side of slot 12, the followed actor;
#   `$1f36..$1f54` — `actor_table_reset`, all nineteen records of one table marked free;
#   `$2af2..$2b0a` — `actor_start_motion_at_speed`, the launch (three flag bits and a speed byte);
#   `$2b5a..$2bc8` — the three step-reaction routines, `actor_hop_or_flip_side` / `_toggle_side_flag`
#     / `_turn_and_launch`, which read the map steps' own outcome byte and ground flags. GHIDRA HAS
#     ONE FUNCTION HERE AND IT IS THE MIDDLE ONE (`F 0x2b82`, 20 bytes, folding in the shared tail
#     at `$2b7a`); `$2b5a` and `$2b8e` are in no F record at all, so this `hi` is `$2b8e + 58`,
#     read off the reconstructed bodies, and the range still claims exactly one ENTRY.
0x2af2
0x2b5a
0x5e3e
# The actor tier (batch 8): nineteen 32-byte records in one of three parallel tables, projected
# once a frame into nineteen 6-byte screen records. `$67c2`/`$67e0`/`$67f8` are the entry tier
# (three F rows, `$67c2..$6822`); `$8dfe`/`$8e66` are the two projection passes (`$8dfe..$8f02`),
# which share 68 identical bytes. Five functions, 356 bytes, all reconstructed and green.
# The respawn continuation (batch 22, the row batch 22b drafted): `actor_respawn_as_new_kind`
# ($6cdc..0x6d5a, 126 B) is what a defeated slot comes back as -- reached from ONE place, the
# `ble.w $6cdc` at $6c34 inside `actor_defeat_and_score`, so it is a continuation rather than a
# subroutine, and it ends in the `rts` that returns to THAT routine's caller. It became its own
# F record only when `../names.txt` named it: the pre-2026-08-07 scan folded it into $6bb8's
# 290-byte body. Its caller $6bb8 is deliberately NOT here -- see PORTABILITY.md §0h.
0x6cdc
# The background scroll ENGINE (batches 5-6): fifteen F rows tile `$7522..$8228` — the queue
# drain, the four axis steps, the two row fills and the pre-shift — and fill the eight
# pre-shifted buffers that `bg_scroll_blit` below then copies to the screen. Filed under the
# "game logic" catch-all until the 2026-08-02 re-measure; producer and consumer are one subsystem.
0x8dfe
# 0x8f02 joined this range in batch 15: sprite_draw_pass is the twelve blitters' only caller and
# the tier is one story end to end (recreate/STATUS.md, batch 15). Re-measure queued as usual.
# The text subsystem (batches 8-9): `$bd8a` (the message-box lifecycle) plus the plotter's two
# entry points `$bf4e`/`$bf5e`, which are one routine — `$bf4e` has no `rts` and falls through.
# Three F rows tile `$bd8a..$c030` exactly, and `$c030` is architecture.md's own CODE/DATA
# boundary. Its one caller is `game_main_loop` and it calls nothing outside itself.
# The HUD partition (batch 18, the measurement queued since batch 15 and unblocked by 16b): the
# status panel is one subsystem, cited from the batches' own reads that the cluster TILES — the
# pass and its ten callees plus every tier under them ($b346..$bd66, batches 2-4/13/16b; the range
# ends at hud_draw_two_digits' body end, $bd66..$bd8a being the panel's own state words), the
# region-restore family the pass opens with ($d93a..$dbb0, batch 4; NOT $dbc0, unported game
# logic), the effect/state stubs that WRITE the panel's slots, meter and state words
# ($10200..$103e8, batch 1 — the queue entry's own list), and hud_draw_lives ($e80c, batch 13).
# The SCENE tier (batch 20, the measurement batch 19 queued): scene_run_frame + its budget helper
# ($dbc0..$df9e, ending at actor_slots_mark_free's entry — batch 19's read is the citation) and
# scene_exit_and_reload ($dfbe..$e026, read+named, unported: its stage_load_window call is the PSG
# wall). NOTE the expected shape: the tier is 2/3 RECONSTRUCTED (to a stop_pc boundary) while the
# whole-function measurement prices $dbc0 T4-transitive through those very tails — the first row
# where the boundary convention makes "reconstructed" exceed "runnable".
0xdbc0
0xdfbe
0xd93a
0xe80c
0xbd8a
# `actor_slots_mark_free` (batch 10): the free-marker walk `actor_table_reset`'s callers use when
# only the markers are to move. One function, 14 bytes, two `bsr` callers.
0xdf9e
# The banner plotters (batch 12): `bg_plot_round_banner` calls `bg_plot_banner` twice, which calls
# `bg_plot_banner_glyph` per character — and all three write BACKGROUND BUFFER COPY 0 at `$44000`,
# the same buffer `bg_build_buffer` fills and `bg_build_preshifted_copies` then derives the other
# seven from. Three F rows tiling `$e110..$e19a` exactly.
# The two stage kind DRAWS (batch 22, the row batch 22b drafted): `stage_random_kind32` ($e1c8,
# 40 B) and `stage_random_kind8` ($e1f0, 50 B) pick which creature a respawned slot comes back as,
# out of the current stage_number's candidate table. ONE range covering both, deliberately NOT
# split at $e1f0: $e1c8 has no tail of its own and `bra.w $e214` INTO $e1f0's, so the fourteen
# bytes $e214..$e221 belong to both routines and recreate/src/rng.c spells them once. Splitting
# here would draw a subsystem boundary through the middle of an instruction sequence both
# routines execute. `hi` is $e1f0's body_end, per this file's rule. $e1c8 became its own F record
# only when `../names.txt` named it -- the pre-2026-08-07 scan had no entry for it at all.
0xe1c8
0xe7f4
# `$e80c..$e87c` IS NOT BOOT and used to be filed as it: it is `hud_draw_lives` (batch 13), whose
# one caller is `game_life_restart_reset`. There is no status-panel subsystem in this file, so it
# falls to the catch-all with the rest of the HUD rather than into a one-function bucket of its
# own — see PORTABILITY.md §0b, which registers that as the largest remaining mis-partition.
0xe87c
0xecba
0xf8bc
# The STAGE tier (batch 12), what runs when a stage or a game starts:
#   `$f95c..$fa2e` — `stage_load_window`, the loader's top: it latches the map and start pointers,
#     calls the three builders below back to back, sets the palette and starts the stage's tune
#     (the last two are why it is not reconstructed);
#   `$fe4a..$ff42` — `game_restart_reset` falling through into `game_life_restart_reset` (one F
#     row, two routines with an entrant each) and `stage_reset_state`, the per-stage state reset.
0xf95c
# The three routines that FILL the buffers the scroll engine then maintains (batch 12), which is
# why they are background scroll and not stage: `bg_build_buffer` draws the map's window into
# copy 0, `stage_publish_scroll_state` writes the very limits, cursors, position words and sixteen
# row pointers `$7522`'s engine steps, and `bg_build_preshifted_copies` derives copies 1..7.
# Two ranges, not one: `$fc46..$fd46` between them is the eight 32-byte palettes, i.e. data.
0xfa30
0xfd46
# `resource_table_relocate` (batch 12): turns the leading offset of each 20-byte record of the
# disk-loaded table at `$248d8` into an absolute pointer, once, behind its own `'E'` signature
# byte. Its single caller is `show_data_disk_prompt`, the same boot routine that drives
# `load_resource_by_index` above, and its two operand addresses are touched only from that path.
0xfe1e
0xfe4a
# The spawn tier (batch 13): `actor_spawn_pass` walks the published template table and spawns from
# it, `actor_spawn_from_template` turns a 32-byte template into an actor record, and
# `actor_template_set_hitpoints` writes the difficulty ramp back into the template. Three F rows
# tiling `$ff42..$1009a` exactly, and `$1009a` is architecture.md's own CODE/DATA boundary.
0xff42
0x17adc
